solution: Solution: Let $A$ be the event that candidate A gets the job and $B$ be the event that candidate B gets the job. It is given that $P(A)=0.8$ and $P(B)=0.7$ . Assuming the selections are independent, $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)=0.8\times 0.7=0.56$ . The probability that at least one of them gets the job is $P(A\cup B)$ . By the addition theorem, $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$ . Thus, $P(A\cup B)=0.8+0.7-0.56=0.94$ . Hence, the correct answer is $0.94$ . © examsnet.com

subject: Chemistry
question: An alcohol $X(\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{12}\mathrm{O})$ on dehydration gives Y (major product). Reaction of Y with HBr gave $Z(\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{Br}.)$ , major product). Z undergoes nucleophilic substitution in two steps. What are X and Y ? [AP EAPCET 26 May 2025 S1]

answer_provenance.method: single green option label (RGB 0,128,0); four option labels required

solution: Solution: Identify Z: Since Z undergoes nucleophilic substitution in two steps, it follows an $\mathrm{S_N1}$ mechanism, so Z must be a tertiary alkyl bromide. For the formula $\mathrm{C}_5\mathrm{H}_{11}\mathrm{Br}$ , the tertiary bromide is 2-bromo-2-methylbutane, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(Br)CH_2CH_3}$ . Identify Y: HBr addition to Y gives this tertiary bromide by Markovnikov addition, so Y is 2-methylbut-2-ene, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CHCH_3}$ . Identify X: Dehydration of X must give 2-methylbut-2-ene as the major product. The alcohol that directly gives this more substituted alkene is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C(OH)CH_2CH_3}$ . Mechanism check: Z ionizes slowly to a tertiary carbocation and $\mathrm{Br^-}$ , then the nucleophile attacks in a fast second step, confirming two-step $\mathrm{S_N1}$ substitution. Thus X is 2-methylbutan-2-ol and Y is 2-methylbut-2-ene, which corresponds to option option B. © examsnet.com
